sections.label: Construction Work Permit holder numbers and wages
sections.summary: Construction Work Permit holder numbers fell about 15% from pre-COVID-19 levels, while median wages in March were 15% to 30% higher.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Compared to pre-COVID-19 levels, the number of construction Work Permit holders has dropped by about 15%, and the number is projected to fall in the months ahead given the on-going COVID-19 situation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Based on MOM's data on construction Work Permit holder salaries, median wages in March this year were 15% to 30% higher compared to pre-COVID-19 levels due to competition for the limited supply of workers within the sector.

sections.label: Delayed HDB BTO projects
sections.summary: More than eight in 10 on-going HDB BTO projects were delayed by about six to nine months beyond their originally indicated Estimated Completion Dates.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: For example, we had previously shared that more than eight in 10 of on-going HDB BTO projects have been delayed by about six to nine months beyond the Estimated Completion Dates originally indicated to flat owners during project launches.

sections.label: Levy rebates and PRC worker entry
sections.summary: Foreign Worker Levy rebates for Work Permit holders rose from $90 to $250 per worker monthly from May to December 2021, and new PRC construction Work Permit holders may enter first and test locally.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Third, we have increased the existing Foreign Worker Levy rebates for Work Permit holders from $90 per worker per month to $250 per worker per month, for the period May to December 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: But the crux of the current problem is limited inflow of workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Hence, fourth, we will temporarily allow new PRC construction Work Permit holders to enter Singapore to work first and take their skills certification tests locally, instead of in China.

sections.label: COVID-19 Temporary Measures Amendment Bill
sections.summary: The COVID-19 (Temporary Measures) (Amendment No 3) Bill seeks to facilitate sharing of foreign manpower cost increases between project parties.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: At the same time, there is still a need to provide support for existing construction projects, where parties may not have adequately priced in the unexpected increase in foreign manpower costs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: That is why we are introducing the COVID-19 (Temporary Measures) (Amendment No 3) Bill this evening.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The Bill seeks to facilitate sharing of the increase in foreign manpower costs between project parties.

sections.label: Scope of relief period
sections.summary: New section 79C specifies the relief period from 1 October 2020 to 30 September 2021, or any extended prescribed date.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The new section 79C sets out the scope of the relief.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: This specifies the period subject to relief, which will be from 1 October 2020 to 30 September 2021, or any extended date as may be prescribed, to tie in with the current end points of relief periods under Part 2 and Part 8B of the Act.

sections.label: Adjusting contract sums for manpower costs
sections.summary: The proposed amendments aim to let parties such as contractors apply to adjust the contract sum for foreign manpower cost increases.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The proposed amendments to the COVID-19 (Temporary Measures) Act aim to allow parties, such as contractors, to apply to adjust the contract sum for their projects in view of the foreign manpower cost increases.

sections.label: Construction alliances and funding support
sections.summary: The alliance approach aims to uplift the construction value chain, with the Growth and Transformation Scheme rolled out with a few alliances first, and the CPCF extended to March 2022 with 80% PIP co-funding.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: This alliance approach seeks to uplift the entire value chain because, given the heavy interdependencies between different segments of the value chain in construction, it is difficult for any one firm to effect significant transformation entirely on its own.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We plan to roll out the Growth and Transformation Scheme with a few alliances first, starting in the second half of this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We have also extended the Construction Productivity and Capability Fund, or CPCF, by one year until March 2022, and will maintain the enhanced co-funding support of 80% under the Productivity Innovation Project, or PIP scheme.

sections.label: Removal of Man-Year-Entitlement framework
sections.summary: The Man-Year-Entitlement framework is intended to be removed in the near future and replaced with a system incentivising more productive off-site work.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: As previously announced, we intend to remove the Man-Year-Entitlement (MYE) framework in the near future and replace it with a system that incentivises more productive off-site work.

sections.label: COVID-19 relief for construction contracts
sections.summary: The Bill seeks to provide relief for businesses undertaking construction works under construction contracts affected by a rise in foreign manpower salary costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The construction sector, like many others, has been hard hit by COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This Bill seeks to provide relief for businesses undertaking construction works under construction contracts that have been affected by a rise in foreign manpower salary costs.

sections.label: Concern over misuse of COVID-19 reason
sections.summary: It would undermine the legislation's purpose if companies cite COVID-19 for higher foreign manpower costs while deploying foreign manpower to new projects and letting pre-1 October 2020 contracts proceed slowly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To that end, it would undermine the purpose of this legislation if some companies, particularly larger ones, cite COVID-19 as a reason for higher foreign manpower costs resulting in increased cost for contracting parties or even the public, while at the same time deploying foreign manpower to start on new projects even as their contracts that predate the 1 October 2020 are allowed to proceed slowly, when they may instead be completed forthwith.

sections.label: Higher Work Permit holder rebate
sections.summary: The rebate for each Work Permit holder in the Construction, Marine and Process sectors will go up from $90 to $250 per month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: First, Mdm Deputy Speaker, we need to continue to help the industry with labour costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It is good to know that the rebate for each Work Permit holder in the Construction, Marine and Process sectors will go up from $90 to $250 per month.

sections.label: Rising raw material costs
sections.summary: While scrambling for workers, companies also face raw material costs rising by 30% to 40% as projects drag on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: While they are scrambling for workers, they are also facing the rising cost of raw materials, which are going up by 30% to 40%, as the projects drag on.

sections.label: Support based on demonstrated harm
sections.summary: The speaker questions why smaller sectors were excluded and suggests amendments cover all firms demonstrating harm rather than by economic sector.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While I recognise that these are comparatively smaller sectors, it is unclear why these have not been considered for additional support, even if they may be similarly afflicted.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It strikes me as more sensible to allow for the coverage of these amendments to apply to all firms that are able to demonstrate harm rather than by economic sector per se.

sections.label: Worker losses from expiring permits
sections.summary: In the second half of 2020, about 41,500 workers were lost due to expiring permits.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Indeed, in the second half of 2020, we lost some 41,500 workers due to expiring permits.

sections.label: Worker transfer and exchange suggestions
sections.summary: Gerald Giam suggested transfers from day 56, and the speaker suggests employers release NTS workers directly to the exchange.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: My Aljunied GRC colleague, Mr Gerald Giam, had previously suggested to this House that workers should be permitted to request a transfer as early as the 56th day, the same time that the employer is required to renew.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Another suggestion that I am presenting today is to mandate the employers who wish to otherwise send their NTS workers home, to instead release them directly to the exchange.

sections.label: Costs of low-cost foreign worker model
sections.summary: Managing COVID-19 with a large low-cost foreign workforce reveals external costs and weak productivity incentives, so capital-labour deployment should be monitored.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The challenges – and dare we say additional cost – of managing COVID-19 in the presence of a large low-cost foreign worker workforce reveal that there are additional costs external to each firm that are not fully accounted for when we rely on this labour-intensive model.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Moreover, by keeping wages low in this sector, there is limited incentive to rapidly scale up productivity, whether in terms of attaining modern construction skills or adopting appropriate safety-related best practices or acquiring new equipment and machinery.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The result could be reduced quality of our constructed buildings – a factor not well captured by the dollars and cents reflected in project costing.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: If so, we would do well to carefully monitor the capital-labour deployment in the industry over the next few years and, if proven efficacious for raising productivity, consider implementing measures to support high wages in this sector.

sections.label: Independent assessor for manpower costs
sections.summary: Under the Bill, an independent assessor assesses foreign manpower cost increases, paid mainly by the property developer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Under the Bill, an independent assessor is appointed to assess the foreign manpower cost increase as a result of the tight migrant worker situation and the assessed cost is to be paid by the property developer, mainly.

sections.label: Raising ABSD to reduce foreign demand
sections.summary: Increasing Additional Buyer Stamp Duty is proposed to reduce foreign demand, dampen the property market and raise revenue for contractor relief.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In addition, for our people, especially the younger couples planning to start a family who are facing a housing shortage and a long Build-To-Order (BTO) queue at the moment, it would also be good policy to rein in the aggressive property purchases by foreigners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Hence, a more appropriate solution is to increase the Additional Buyer Stamp Duty (ABSD) to reduce foreigners' demand, dampen the property market and raise revenue to pay for the financial relief for the contractors.

sections.label: Contractors' foreign labour reliance
sections.summary: The problem is partly caused by contractors relying on foreign labour too long, so relief must come with commitment to process redesign and automation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The current problem is partly caused by contractors having relied on foreign labour for far too long.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: So, the relief assistance we give to the contractors must come with commitment from them to accelerate process redesign and automation.

sections.label: ABSD increase for rental units
sections.summary: A bigger ABSD increase may yield enough additional fiscal revenue to provide rental units for Singaporean couples waiting for BTO flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: If the Government dares to take the bold move to make a bigger increase in the ABSD, there may even be enough additional fiscal revenue to provide for rental units for our Singaporean couples who are waiting for their BTO flats.

sections.label: Relief measures and construction transformation
sections.summary: Relief measures can be part of transforming construction, attracting Singaporeans with higher wages, and an ABSD increase can fund housing for couples waiting for HDB flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Government can incorporate relief measures into its strategy to transform the construction sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This is also an excellent opportunity to attract some Singaporeans to rejoin the construction industry, as contractors now can pay higher wages to Singaporean workers, considering the substantial increase in foreign workers' wages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: If the Government boldly increases ABSD, there will be enough additional revenue to provide housing for Singaporean couples waiting for HDB flats, so that we can maintain the pace of family formation and Total Fertility Rate, prevent future population gaps and not leave the next generation with another problem.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: With our proposed increase in ABSD, limiting the number of foreign workers will not worsen our lives.

sections.label: Local manpower and contract adjustment Bill
sections.summary: The model develops local human resource and cuts foreign workers over time, while the Bill lets contractors adjust sums of uncompleted contracts amid a manpower crunch.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This model will focus on developing and training our well-educated local human resource and strategically bringing down the number of foreign workers over time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We urge the Government to consider our proposal seriously and amend this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The latest whiplash comes from the surge of cases in India.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It has forced us to bar entry for all work pass holders from there.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This means the industry’s manpower crunch will continue and even worsen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This Bill allows contractors to adjust the monetary sums of contracts that have not yet been completed.

sections.label: China workers' skills certification
sections.summary: For six months, workers from China can obtain their skills certification in Singapore rather than in their home country.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For six months, workers from China can obtain their skills certification in Singapore rather than in their home country.

sections.label: Bill's effect on construction spending
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Bill will result in the Government spending more on construction projects than previously expected as contract sums are adjusted upwards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Will this Bill result in the Government ending up spending more on construction projects than previously expected, as contract sums get adjusted upwards?

sections.label: COVID-19 pandemic trade-offs
sections.summary: The COVID-19 pandemic has presented Singapore with two important trade-offs, the first being between saving jobs and protection from the virus.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The COVID-19 pandemic has presented Singapore with two important trade-offs.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The first trade-off is between the saving of jobs and protection from the virus.

sections.label: International integration versus pandemic control
sections.summary: The second trade-off is between international economic integration and national control of the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The second trade-off is between international economic integration and national control of the pandemic.

sections.label: Bill enactment adapting to pandemic
sections.summary: The enactment of this Bill reflects effort to adapt to unforeseen circumstances that the evolving pandemic will continue to present.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The enactment of this Bill reflects our effort to adapt to unforeseen circumstances that this evolving pandemic will continue to present to us.

sections.label: Construction workforce reduction
sections.summary: Even before the recent halt to new incoming migrant workers from the Indian subcontinent, many construction companies saw their workforce reduced by 15% to 30% due to higher than usual attrition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Even before the recent halt to new incoming migrant workers from the Indian subcontinent, many construction companies saw their workforce reduced by 15% to 30% due to higher than usual attrition.

sections.label: Pre-COVID-19 projects and labour shortage
sections.summary: Pre-COVID-19 projects are languishing as everybody is worried about their viability, and due to labour shortage some workers ask for daily wages of more than $250.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Pre-COVID-19 projects are languishing as everybody is worried about the viability of these projects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: And because of the labour shortage, we are seeing some workers asking for daily wages of more than $250.

sections.label: Iron ore price increase
sections.summary: For example, the price of iron ore has shot up more than 27% since the end of last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: For example, the price of iron ore has shot up more than 27% since the end of last year.

sections.label: Manpower cost sharing and levy rebate
sections.summary: Sharing extra manpower costs from project delays and a $250 manpower levy rebate help the industry's financial sustainability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: First, the sharing of the extra manpower costs from project delays as well as the manpower levy rebate of $250 are extremely helpful to the financial sustainability of the industry.

sections.label: Postponing projects and larger levy rebates
sections.summary: If labour shortage continues, new infrastructure projects could be postponed; if conditions worsen, the industry hopes for larger levy rebates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Three, should the labour shortage continue, we can consider postponing new infrastructure projects, at least the big ones, or at least the construction phase of these new projects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Four, if the industry condition worsens, the industry hopes that the Government can provide added support with larger levy rebates.

sections.label: New circuit breaker contingency plan measures
sections.summary: A new circuit breaker contingency plan could include onsite teams, no contact between contractor groups, limited subcontractor site entry, and other measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: A new contingency plan for circuit breaker could include measures, such as: (a) Main contractors, builders to have teams permanently onsite with workers who are also lodging in the dormitories onsite; (b) Main contractor workers to have no in-person contact with sub-contractor workers; (c) Subcontractor workers may enter a site for a maximum of three days a week only; (d) Subcontractor workers should not be allowed to lodge onsite; (e) All non-essential roles to be fully working from home; and (f) Permitting TLQ (Temporary Living Quarters) again for larger projects.

sections.label: Further extensions beyond six-month extension
sections.summary: The Government has provided a six-month extension, but MOF can consider further extensions if necessary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: The Government has already provided a six-month extension, but MOF can consider further extensions, if necessary.

sections.label: Assessors consider support in adjudicating claims
sections.summary: When adjudicating claims, Assessors will consider support already provided, such as foreign worker levy rebates, in determining a just manpower cost-sharing outcome.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: When adjudicating claims, the Assessors will take into consideration the amount of support that has already been provided, such as foreign worker levy rebates and other forms of support, in determining what a just and equitable outcome of manpower cost-sharing should be.

sections.label: ABSD remission timeline extension suggestion
sections.summary: Mr Henry Kwek suggested extending the ABSD remission timeline for developers; earlier extensions were given for PCP, ABSD commencement and completion, and sale.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Mr Henry Kwek suggested extending the Additional Buyer’s Stamp Duty (ABSD) remission timeline for developers, to relieve pressure on them, too.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We had earlier provided a 12-month extension of the PCP and ABSD remission timeline for commencement and completion and a six-month extension to the remission timeline for sale, to account for delays due to COVID-19.

sections.label: Temporary flexibility for PRC workers
sections.summary: BCA worked with MOM to roll out temporary flexibility to facilitate entry of PRC Work Permit holders, and will discuss extending it to other source countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Taking this feedback onboard, BCA worked with MOM to roll out this temporary flexibility to help facilitate the entry of PRC Work Permit holders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: BCA will discuss with the industry to assess if this approach can be extended to workers from other approved source countries and examine carefully this proposal.

sections.label: Work permit age and work hours
sections.summary: MOM allows renewals up to age 60, assesses appeals case-by-case for workers above 50, and the Employment Act caps normal work at 44 hours weekly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: To clarify, MOM already allows existing Work Permit holders to renew their work permits with their current employers up to the age of 60.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: For workers above the age of 50 who wish to change employers but are unable to do so due to the age limit, MOM will assess appeals on a case-by-case basis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: As for working longer hours, it is important for workers to get sufficient rest for their well-being and their safety.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: And that is why the Employment Act stipulates that the normal hours of work should not exceed 44 hours per week.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In addition, employers must not make their employees work for more than 12 hours a day, including overtime, with a limit of 72 hours of overtime in a month.

sections.label: Suite of support measures
sections.summary: The grants in the Construction Productivity and Capability Fund, the new Growth and Transformation Scheme and the PIP scheme form a suite of measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: All these efforts, including the grants in the Construction Productivity and Capability Fund (CPCF), the new Growth and Transformation Scheme, our PIP scheme – all these are a suite of measures.

sections.label: BCA Industry Scholarship for Singaporeans
sections.summary: BCA awards an Industry Scholarship yearly to Singaporeans in ITE, Polytechnic and University, paying more than 80% of their studies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: As for Mr Leong Mun Wai's sense that there are no efforts to bring Singaporeans into this sector, apart from asking him to read Minister of State Tan Kiat How's speech outlining those efforts, precisely those efforts, just a few months ago, I would also share that we have a BCA Industry Scholarship year after year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We award to Singaporeans in ITE, Polytechnic and University, scholarships for young, bright, energetic, Singaporeans who want to venture into this sector, into architecture, into building, into M&E, into the digital space for construction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We pay the bulk of the scholarship, more than 80% of their studies.

sections.label: Legislating sharing of additional costs
sections.summary: The question raised is whether legislation should be passed to facilitate sharing of additional costs that increased beyond contractors' expectations when they bid.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: What we are saying is that because the costs have increased beyond their expectation at the point in time when they bidded for these contracts, should we or should we not pass legislation to facilitate the sharing of these additional costs?

sections.label: Construction sector and Bill support
sections.summary: The construction sector touches Singaporeans' lives on almost every front, and Mr Leong Mun Wai is asked whether he supports the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: This is so, even in the construction sector, but especially in this sector, which is so interwoven, which touches Singaporeans' lives on almost every front: building of your homes, building of your roads, building of your public transport, building of the facilities, including the medical facilities that are so critical in the fight against COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: And so, I ask Mr Leong Mun Wai, because I seem to get the sense from him that he does not support this Bill, does not support bearing some of the burden that Singapore contractors are suffering under, does not support bringing in foreign workers in order to help the sector cope during this period.

sections.label: ABSD and HDB rental flats
sections.summary: He raises points about cooling the property market with ABSD and using the money for cost increases and HDB rental flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: And he makes a number of other points and I am tussling over whether to spend more of this evening, during the Second Reading to address them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: But he talks about cooling the property market by increasing the ABSD and then taking that money to pay for the cost increases and then using the money also to fund more HDB rental flats.

sections.label: Singapore staying connected to the world
sections.summary: Singapore needs to preserve jobs and capabilities by staying connected to the world, and will monitor economic and global health situations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Unlike some other countries, Singapore needs to preserve jobs and capabilities by staying connected to the world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We will continue to carefully monitor the economic situation as well as the global health situation and make adjustments as necessary.

sections.label: Foreign workers and dire situations
sections.summary: For these individuals the situation is dire, so it would be unfair to stop foreign workers from coming in right now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: So, for these particular individuals, it is a dire situation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: And, so, it would be grossly unfair then to suddenly pull the rug from under their feet and say, no, we have to stop foreign workers from coming in right now.

sections.label: Assistance tied to construction improvements
sections.summary: He asks whether assistance to construction companies ties them down for future process improvements, automation and employing local workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: The other thing is that when we give all this assistance to the construction companies, do we actually tie the companies down for future improvements in their processes and automation, and also employing our local workers?

sections.label: Need for some foreign workers
sections.summary: Even with automation and productivity, some foreign workers will still be needed to supplement the core of Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: At the end of the day, even as we automate, even as we increase productivity – as both Mr Leong Mun Wai and Assoc Prof Jamus Lim say we should – there will still be a need for some foreign workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We will keep them in our sector, keep them here, to supplement the core of Singaporeans that we want to build for the sector.

sections.label: Doing away with MYE framework
sections.summary: They recognise the pain, but significant moves start next year, including doing away with the MYE framework for more productive offsite work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: They recognise that this is going to be painful.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: But we will make some significant moves starting from next year, including doing away with the MYE framework, moving to one in which it biases towards more productive offsite work.

sections.label: Foreign worker skills and wages
sections.summary: Offsite foreign workers must be more skilled to operate machinery, so wages will be higher, and the dependency ratio ceiling will be tightened.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: But even those foreign workers working offsite will have to be more skilled to operate the machinery and, therefore, the wages will have to be higher – because they are more productive and more skilled.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: But the same time, we will also tighten on the dependency ratio ceiling.

sections.label: Contractors concerned about worker poaching
sections.summary: Contractors, including small subcontractors, are most concerned and unhappy about worker poaching over recent months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: If you speak with contractors, including the small subcontractors that the Leader of the Opposition has spoken to, what they are most concerned about and unhappy about over the last few months, is precisely worker poaching.

sections.label: Stopping worker poaching
sections.summary: With worker scarcity and projects at stake, poaching needs to be stopped within appropriate limits, and Dr Tan See Leng can address MOM questions later.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: I think Dr Tan See Leng can come in later if the Member would like to ask MOM more about this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: But now, with worker scarcity, with projects at stake, it is precisely the opposite that needs to be done, within appropriate limits, ensuring that this poaching gets put to a stop.      .
